proves: A check-then-act race introduced by this change.

expectedFindings.quote:
const current = await store.get(key);
  await store.set(key, current + 1);
expectedFindings.rationale:
An atomic increment on the store was replaced by a read-then-write with an `await` between the two halves. Two concurrent callers both read the same value and both write the same increment, so one is lost.

NOTE: this replaced a version whose stated finding was a lost-update race — but the read-modify-write race was *pre-existing* in the pre-image, so the change did not cause it. Worse, it missed the obvious: the replacement guarded the write behind `if (current === 0)`, so the counter would have been stuck at 1 forever. Verified: three increments yield 1. The held-out fixture was measuring a pre-existing subtlety while ignoring a blatant sequential bug in the line being added.

expectedNoFindings: Returning `current + 1` matches the returned value the atomic version gave.

forbiddenFindings.reason: the atomic call is what was removed, not a defect
